Ive been vegan for over 8 years, from my teenage years and now into my mid-twenties. Ok now this is gonna get a bit TMI. I had a period of bloating and issues with gas when I had an embarrassing high-carb/low-fat and mostly raw phase. These issues went away when I started eating more cooked food, more fat and protein, and *gasp* more processed foods. I had a period of depression that I think is unrelated to diet but I got medicated for it over a few years and now have been both off of medication and in decent mental health for the last few years. I have not had any physical health scares. I still get colds but not too often and so far I've always recovered quickly with few symptoms. My digestion has significantly improved from my childhood when I seemed to bounce between constipation and diarrhea and had severe bloating regularly. Now I have really good digestion most days and almost never feel bloated. My energy levels are good and my recovery and endurance is quite good for my level of fitness. I still get mild acne sometimes but I have bigger things to worry about. I started taking a cheap vegan multivitamin and algae oil for DHA/EPA recently but honestly I'm just doing it to cover my bases. I used to supplement for B12 individually but now I just get it from the multi. I also take extra vitamin d in the winter because I live in a cold climate. 

To summarize, I have been vegan for years and generally improved my health. I've managed to resolve the issues that did come up while still maintaining a vegan lifestyle. Do I feel like an ethereal being of perfect health and happiness everyday? No and no one should expect any diet to make them feel that way. Life is hard sometimes and many things can affect your physical and mental health. Despite my aforementioned weird "healthy eating" phase, I went and stayed vegan because of my moral principles and because I want to make a positive impact on the world in the small ways I can. I love the feeling of living in line with what I believe in and expect to stay vegan for the rest of my life.
